thoughts: The terms are named for their role in a load path, not their form: a grommet, an earing, a reef point, a bowsie — you cannot tell what they are by looking, only by what they hold and the tension they carry.
Two kinds of tension element sit side by side: a bowsie tunes tension smoothly under load; a tenterhook pins cloth stretched and immobile. A tuner versus a fixture.
tenterhook escapes the workshop: 'on tenterhooks' turns a cloth-stretcher into the name of a felt state — held taut, in suspense.

thoughts: Grounding the triplet (force/restraint -> affect) in the substrate: 'wound' HOLDS it — 'injury by which the skin is divided' vs 'to hurt a person's feelings' at cos 0.43, two distinct senses under one word node. The migration I predicted is real for wound.

But the substrate's lowest min_inter pairs are not that migration at all: 'shock' 0.15 is shaggy-lapdog vs geological crystal deformation; 'strain' 0.166 is a deer's track vs to stretch; 'taut' 0.171 is nautical discipline vs a wine term. These are obscure homonyms, not live metaphor.
'tenterhook' has a single sense node — the idiom lives in the phrase, not the word — so the word-anchored scan cannot see it. My neat bridge was partly an artefact of how I wanted it to read.
